c.tagline: Korea's soul-food capital, where 800 hanok houses cradle the birthplace of bibimbap.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and cheap; most residents summon them through the Kakao T app, which shows the fare and lets you pay by registered card. Street hails are also easy in the center.

emergency.note: Dial 112 for police and 119 for fire or ambulance; the 1330 Korea Travel Hotline offers 24/7 English assistance.

hood_desc: The famous cluster of more than 800 traditional tile-roofed hanok houses, home to Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Jeondong Catholic Cathedral, hanji paper workshops, and endless street food; the sightseeing core where most visitors base themselves.
The modern downtown north of the hanok quarter around the historic Gaeksa guesthouse pavilion, thick with shops, cafes, cosmetics stores, and youthful nightlife; best for shopping and going out.
A sprawling traditional market on the edge of the hanok village, famous by day for produce and by night for its Youth Mall food stalls and makgeolli alleys; a paradise for market snacking.
A calmer district north of the center built around Deokjin Park and its lotus-covered pond and university campuses; leafy, local, and relaxed, with cheaper stays.
A hillside neighborhood of steep lanes covered in murals and illustrations inspired by children's stories, dotted with indie cafes and craft shops; arty and photogenic.

water.note: Tap water is safe, though locals commonly drink bottled or filtered.

transit.pay: Buy or top up a T-money or Hanaro transit card at any convenience store (GS25, CU, 7-Eleven) and tap it on city buses for a base fare of about 1,500 won (~US$1.10); cash is accepted but exact change is expected. The same card works nationwide and on taxis.
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5:30am to 11pm; there is no subway, so late-night trips rely on taxis, which are plentiful and inexpensive.
transit.note: Jeonju has no metro — the compact hanok village is best explored on foot, while frequent city buses connect the downtown, Deokjin Park, and Jeonju Station a few kilometres northeast of the center.

train: Jeonju Station (KTX / SRT via Iksan, Jeolla Line)

transit.m: Intercity bus Gunsan–Jeonju + city bus (~90 min)
KTX to Jeonju via Yongsan/Seoul from Gimpo (GMP) area (~2 hr)
Airport limousine bus from Muan Int'l (MWX) via Gwangju

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in South Korea; there is no need to tip taxis, restaurants, or hotels.
